newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela Jan inflation to rise 2.0 pct - Petkoff.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela Jan inflation to rise 2.0 pct - Petkoff.

text.p: Venezuela's inflation rate in January is expected to be 2.0 percent, down from 3.0 percent in December 1996, Planning Minister Teodoro Petkoff said Friday.

"Taking into account rate hikes for the (Caracas) metro and (telephone company) CANTV, we estimate inflation in January to be around two percent," he told reporters at Miraflores presidential palace after the weekly cabinet meeting.
Inflation, which was 8.1 percent in January 1996, topped last year at 103.2 percent, a Venezuelan record and also one for Latin America in 1996.
Petkoff said that "by maintaining fiscal discipline and with the understanding of all sectors," the country should be able in 1997 "to reach the goal of 25 percent inflation."
He urged all sectors of public life to limit wage claims that could fuel inflation.
Petkoff also noted that the December figure, announced Thursday by the Central Bank, showed that "structurally, inflation is receding."
It peaked at 12.6 percent in May shortly after the implementation of an IMF-inspired economic reform program.
Although inflation closed 1996 in triple digits and at a record high, the December figure was the lowest of the year.
